# AIVIA configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `aivia config docs`; do not edit by hand. -->
<!-- Regenerate: aivia config docs --output docs/CONFIG.md -->

This reference is generated from the registered configuration models, their JSON Schema and model docstrings. Every top-level key is one section; unknown keys are rejected. Values may reference environment variables as `${NAME}` or `${NAME:-default}`.

## Root keys

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | integer | Configuration schema version. |
| `accessibility` | [AccessibilityConfig](#accessibility) or null | Alt text, subtitles and contrast settings for accessible outputs. |
| `api` | [ApiConfig](#api) or null | The local HTTP API bind address, authentication and request limits. |
| `brand` | [BrandKitConfig](#brand) or null | Colours, fonts, logo, watermark, intro/outro and caption style. |
| `budget` | [BudgetConfig](#budget) or null | Spending caps, provider monthly limits, alert thresholds and policy. |
| `character` | [CharacterConfig](#character) or null | Consistency chain, QA thresholds, consent flags and reference limit. |
| `circuit` | [CircuitBreakerConfig](#circuit) or null | Failure threshold and cooldown for one provider circuit. |
| `database` | [DatabaseConfig](#database) or null | The SQLite file inside the user data directory and its busy timeout. ``filename`` is a bare file name; the directory is always the user data directory so a config file cannot point the database at another location. ``busy_timeout_ms`` is how long SQLite waits for a lock before raising ``database is locked``. |
| `delivery` | [DeliveryConfig](#delivery) or null | Delivery providers, the fallback chain and shared retry settings. Providers may be nested under ``providers`` or written directly as ``folder``, ``link``, ``email`` and ``webhook`` keys. The ``chain`` lists provider names in fallback order and every entry must name a provider. |
| `embeddings` | [EmbeddingsConfig](#embeddings) or null | Provider chain, vector dimensions, batching, cache size and model prices. ``chain`` is ordered from most to least preferred and rejects duplicates so a typo never silently changes routing. ``pricing`` values are USD per million input tokens; a model without an entry falls back to the provider metadata and the router's pricing overrides. |
| `formats` | [FormatsConfig](#formats) or null | Named format recipes. Recipes may be written directly under the section (``formats: {narrated_still: {...}}``) or nested under ``formats`` (or ``recipes``); every form validates to the same mapping. |
| `http` | [HttpClientConfig](#http) or null | Retry, backoff and timeout policy for :class:`~aivia.core.http.HttpClient`. |
| `jobs` | [JobsConfig](#jobs) or null | Worker concurrency, retry, heartbeat and run-lock settings. ``concurrency`` is the number of workers. ``max_parallel_runs`` is the global limit on runs holding a lock at once across every profile and process, so scheduled runs cannot overlap unsafely. ``retry_delay_seconds`` is the wait after the first failed attempt, multiplied by ``backoff_multiplier`` on each later attempt and capped by ``max_retry_delay_seconds``. |
| `languages` | [LanguagesConfig](#languages) or null | The available languages plus the one used when none is requested. A config file may write the language entries directly under the section (``languages: {en: {...}, de: {...}}``) or nest them under ``languages``; both forms validate to the same model. |
| `llm` | [LLMConfig](#llm) or null | Provider chain, per-role models, token prices and the repair limit. |
| `models_file` | [ModelsFileConfig](#models_file) or null | The model catalog path, with a documented default of ``models.yaml``. A bare string is accepted as shorthand for ``{path: <string>}`` so the canonical ``models_file: models.yaml`` form in the design stays valid. |
| `occasions` | [OccasionsConfig](#occasions) or null | The configured occasions and the one selected by default. Occasions may be written directly under the section (``occasions: {birthday: {...}}``) or nested under ``occasions``. |
| `orders` | [OrdersConfig](#orders) or null | Personalized order defaults: levels, name verification and pricing. |
| `pipeline` | [PipelineConfig](#pipeline) or null | The ordered stages a pipeline runs and the timezone used for schedules. |
| `planner` | [PlannerConfig](#planner) or null | Step, iteration, approval, tool, preview, default and budget settings. |
| `platforms` | [PlatformsConfig](#platforms) or null | Publishing accounts keyed by ``platform/language``. Entries may be written directly under the section (``platforms: {youtube/en: {...}}``) or nested under ``accounts``. |
| `presets` | [PresetsConfig](#presets) or null | Named presets keyed by name, with an optional default preset. Entries may be written directly under the section (``presets: {short: {...}}``) or nested under ``presets``. |
| `privacy` | [PrivacyConfig](#privacy) or null | Redaction and personal-data handling for logs, prompts and sidecars. |
| `profiles` | [ProfilesConfig](#profiles) or null | Named content profiles. Profiles may be written directly under the section (``profiles: {short: {...}}``) or nested under ``profiles``; both forms validate to the same mapping. |
| `prompts` | [PromptsConfig](#prompts) or null | The selected version of each prompt, with ``auto`` as the fallback. The canonical form is ``prompts: {versions: {image: default}}``. A direct mapping (``prompts: {image: default}``) and aliases such as ``select`` are accepted as well, because the section is small enough that a nesting level should not be a source of configuration errors. |
| `providers` | [ProvidersConfig](#providers) or null | Named provider instances keyed by the names router chains use. Entries may be written directly under the section (``providers: {fal: {...}}``) or nested under ``providers``. Every entry must name a non-empty ``type``. |
| `publish` | [PublishConfig](#publish) or null | Publishing accounts, dry-run policy and reference validation. |
| `quality` | [QualityConfig](#quality) or null | Thresholds and retry policy for generated media quality assurance. |
| `ratelimit` | [RateLimiterConfig](#ratelimit) or null | Default rate and on-limit policy for a provider token bucket. ``requests_per_minute`` is the sustained rate used when a provider does not declare its own limit. ``burst`` is the largest short-term allowance and ``0`` falls back to the sustained rate. ``on_limit`` chooses between waiting for the next token and raising a rate limited error. |
| `reconcile` | [ReconcileConfig](#reconcile) or null | Thresholds that turn an estimate/actual difference into a drift flag. |
| `reference` | [ReferenceConfig](#reference) or null | Similarity level, similarity gates, regeneration cap and downloads. |
| `render` | [RenderConfig](#render) or null | Deterministic renderer settings that never require an AI call. |
| `retention` | [RetentionConfig](#retention) or null | How long intermediates, cache, logs and personal data are kept. Final outputs are pinned and are never removed unless ``delete_final_outputs`` is explicitly enabled. |
| `review` | [ReviewConfig](#review) or null | Approval policy for the optional human review stage. ``approval_mode`` is ``always`` (a reviewer must approve every run), ``ask`` (the default: approve unless a profile says otherwise) or ``never`` (skip the review stage). When a review is not answered before ``timeout_seconds``, ``on_timeout`` decides whether it is rejected, approved or only escalated with a notification. |
| `safety` | [SafetyConfig](#safety) or null | Prompt and media screening before a paid or published call. ``blocked_terms`` holds literal words and phrases that must never reach a paid provider. ``block_categories`` names broader policy categories; the screener treats those names as literal terms too so a category such as ``violence`` is blocked even when no narrower term is configured. |
| `schedule` | [ScheduleConfig](#schedule) or null | Named cron schedules, their timezone and the default entry. Entries may be written directly under the section (``schedule: {daily: {...}}``) or nested under ``schedules``. A single top-level ``cron`` and ``profile`` pair is treated as the ``default`` entry. |
| `scoring` | [ScoringConfig](#scoring) or null | Versioned rubric, dimension weights and score thresholds for research. |
| `storage` | [StorageConfig](#storage) or null | Where generated media and intermediates are stored. Credentials are referenced by name and resolved through the secrets loader, never written into the configuration file. |
| `tracing` | [TracingConfig](#tracing) or null | Optional tracing export; disabled by default and vendor neutral. |
| `video` | [VideoConfig](#video) or null | Video defaults shared by formats, profiles and platform overrides. |

Worker concurrency, retry, heartbeat and run-lock settings. ``concurrency`` is the number of workers. ``max_parallel_runs`` is the global limit on runs holding a lock at once across every profile and process, so scheduled runs cannot overlap unsafely. ``retry_delay_seconds`` is the wait after the first failed attempt, multiplied by ``backoff_multiplier`` on each later attempt and capped by ``max_retry_delay_seconds``.

| `backoff_multiplier` | number | `2.0` | >= 1 |  |

| `heartbeat_seconds` | integer | `30` | > 0 |  |
| `max_attempts` | integer | `3` | >= 1 |  |
| `max_parallel_runs` | integer | `1` | >= 1 |  |
| `max_queue_depth` | integer | `0` | >= 0 |  |
| `max_retry_delay_seconds` | number | `300.0` | >= 0 |  |
| `poll_seconds` | integer | `2` | > 0 |  |
| `retry_delay_seconds` | number | `1.0` | >= 0 |  |
| `stale_after_seconds` | integer | `120` | > 0 |  |

## `ratelimit`

Default rate and on-limit policy for a provider token bucket. ``requests_per_minute`` is the sustained rate used when a provider does not declare its own limit. ``burst`` is the largest short-term allowance and ``0`` falls back to the sustained rate. ``on_limit`` chooses between waiting for the next token and raising a rate limited error.

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `burst` | integer | `0` | >= 0 |  |
| `on_limit` | [OnRateLimit](#onratelimit) | `"wait"` | one of: `wait`, `raise` | What a token bucket does when the next token is not available yet. |
| `requests_per_minute` | integer | `60` | >= 0 |  |

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `drift_threshold` | number | `0.1` | >= 0 | Relative drift above which a reported amount is flagged. |

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |

A cached download is reused unless ``cache`` is disabled. |

## `review`

Approval policy for the optional human review stage. ``approval_mode`` is ``always`` (a reviewer must approve every run), ``ask`` (the default: approve unless a profile says otherwise) or ``never`` (skip the review stage). When a review is not answered before ``timeout_seconds``, ``on_timeout`` decides whether it is rejected, approved or only escalated with a notification.

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_regenerate` | boolean | `true` |  |  |
| `approval_mode` | string | `"ask"` | one of: `always`, `ask`, `never` |  |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` |  |  |
| `max_regenerations` | integer | `3` | >= 0 |  |
| `notify` | boolean | `true` |  |  |
| `on_timeout` | string | `"reject"` | one of: `reject`, `approve`, `notify` |  |
| `preview` | boolean | `true` |  |  |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | `86400` | > 0 |  |

## `safety`

Prompt and media screening before a paid or published call. ``blocked_terms`` holds literal words and phrases that must never reach a paid provider. ``block_categories`` names broader policy categories; the screener treats those names as literal terms too so a category such as ``violence`` is blocked even when no narrower term is configured.

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_regenerate` | boolean | `true` |  |  |
| `block_categories` | array of string |  |  |  |
| `blocked_terms` | array of string |  |  |  |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` |  |  |
| `screen_media` | boolean | `true` |  |  |
| `screen_prompts` | boolean | `true` |  |  |

### StageConfig

One ordered pipeline stage with its recipe-specific options. A stage may be written as a bare string (``write``) or as a mapping with a ``stage``/``name``/``id`` field and an optional ``options`` mapping. The shorthand ``{write: {mode: facts}}`` is accepted too. A mapping may also override the stage class timeout and retry policy through ``timeout_seconds`` or a ``retry_policy`` mapping.

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backoff_multiplier` | number or null | `null` | >= 1 |  |
| `max_attempts` | integer or null | `null` | >= 1 |  |
| `max_retry_delay_seconds` | number or null | `null` | >= 0 |  |
| `options` | object |  |  |  |
| `retry_codes` | array of string or null | `null` |  |  |
| `retry_delay_seconds` | number or null | `null` | >= 0 |  |
| `retry_on_timeout` | boolean or null | `null` |  |  |
| `retry_policy` | [StageRetryPolicy](#stageretrypolicy) or null | `null` |  | How often and how long one stage may run. ``timeout_seconds`` bounds a single attempt; ``None`` disables the deadline. ``max_attempts`` counts the first try, so the default of one means no retries. ``retry_delay_seconds`` is the wait after a failed attempt, multiplied by ``backoff_multiplier`` on each later attempt and capped by ``max_retry_delay_seconds``. ``retry_codes`` adds stable error codes beyond the retryable taxonomy, and ``retry_on_timeout`` controls the per-attempt deadline. |
| `stage` | string |  | length >= 1 |  |
| `timeout_seconds` | number or null | `null` | > 0 |  |

### StageRetryPolicy

How often and how long one stage may run. ``timeout_seconds`` bounds a single attempt; ``None`` disables the deadline. ``max_attempts`` counts the first try, so the default of one means no retries. ``retry_delay_seconds`` is the wait after a failed attempt, multiplied by ``backoff_multiplier`` on each later attempt and capped by ``max_retry_delay_seconds``. ``retry_codes`` adds stable error codes beyond the retryable taxonomy, and ``retry_on_timeout`` controls the per-attempt deadline.

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backoff_multiplier` | number | `1.0` |  |  |
| `max_attempts` | integer | `1` |  |  |
| `max_retry_delay_seconds` | number or null | `null` |  |  |
| `retry_codes` | array of string | `[]` |  |  |
| `retry_delay_seconds` | number | `0.0` |  |  |
| `retry_on_timeout` | boolean | `true` |  |  |
| `timeout_seconds` | number or null | `null` |  |  |

### TokenPricing

USD prices for one million tokens of a model. ``input_per_million`` and ``output_per_million`` are required in spirit but default to zero for backward compatibility. ``cached_input_per_million`` prices prompt tokens a provider served from a cache. Leaving it unset means cached input is charged at the ordinary input price. Whether the provider's reported input count already contains the cached tokens is recorded on :class:`~aivia.providers.protocols.llm.LLMUsage`; the calculator uses that flag so cached tokens are never counted twice.

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cached_input_per_million` | number or null | `null` | >= 0 |  |
| `input_per_million` | number | `0.0` | >= 0 |  |
| `output_per_million` | number | `0.0` | >= 0 |  |

### VariableType

The value type a personalized order variable accepts.

Allowed values: `string`, `text`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `date`, `choice`, `file`, `image`, `audio`, `video`.

### VideoOverridesConfig

Partial video settings applied on top of the base video section.

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `audio_bitrate` | integer or null | `null` | > 0 |  |
| `audio_codec` | string or null | `null` |  |  |
| `bitrate` | integer or null | `null` | > 0 |  |
| `codec` | string or null | `null` |  |  |
| `duration_seconds` | [DurationRangeOverrideConfig](#durationrangeoverrideconfig) or null | `null` |  | A partial duration range used by platform and profile overrides. |
| `fps` | integer or null | `null` | > 0 |  |
| `loudness_lufs` | number or null | `null` |  |  |
| `resolution` | string or null | `null` |  |  |

### WordsPerSecondConfig

Inclusive speaking-rate bounds used to estimate and check script length.

| Key | Type | Default | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max` | number | `3.5` | > 0 |  |
| `min` | number | `2.0` | > 0 |  |
